DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://wv•.w.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 119 s. 2021 October 11, 2021 VICE-MAYOR SOLFERINO A. AGRA, JR. Municipality of Claveria Province of Cagayan Dear Vice-MayorAgra: This has reference to the letter dated 11 June 2021, requesting this Department's legal opinion concerning the designation of Hon. Fredelino D. Agpuldo as Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the Local Chief Executive in your Municipality. As could be gleaned from your letter and its attachments, on 24 May 2021 Municipal Mayor Celia T. Layus issued an Order designating Sangguniang Bayan Member Hon. Fredelino D. Agpuldo as Officer-in-Charge (OIC) of the Office of the Mayor effective 25 to 27 May 2021 pursuant to Section 46 (c) of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC, for brevity). On 25 May 2021, the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) wrote a letter addressed to Mayor Layus through the HRMO averring that the application of Section 46 (c) of the Code to which said designation was anchored is misplaced as it was stated in the said Order that the issuance thereof was due to her leave of absence and not due to travel outside her area of responsibility or jurisdiction. Thus, it is the view of the SB members that the applicable provision of the Code in such case is Section 46 (a) of the Code and not Section 46 (c) thereof. It is also intimated in your letter that Mayor Layus has not been holding her office in the Municipal Hall for over a year now, ostensibly due to her health condition. Apparently, Mayor Layus has been stroke since 13 November 2019. Under such premise, arose your request for this Department's legal opinion on the following issues, which we herein quoted in toto:

1. 2. 3. The propriety of the [Code] provision to which the designation was based; Should the designation be opined valid or invalid, what are the justifications and effect of all transactions that may have transpired and concluded thereon? Should not the LCE, if found in fault, be sanctioned for her inappropriate actions? In reply thereto, we shall address herein queries in one discussion as they are interrelated. At the outset, we deemed it wise to cite herein pertinent provisions of the Code, thus: "Section 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. (a) When the governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice- governor, city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. (b) xxx (c) When the incumbent local chief executive is traveling within the country but outside his territorial jurisdiction for a period not exceeding three (3) consecutive days, he may designate in writing the officer-in-charge of the said office. Such authorization shall specify the powers and functions that the local official concerned shall exercise in the absence of the local chief executive except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees. (d) xxx (e) xxx" (Emphasis supplied).

Based on the aforecited provisions of the LGC, Section 46 (a) contemplates a situation where the local chief executive, in the herein case, the Municipal Mayor, is temporarily incapacitated to perform his/her duties for physical or legal reasons, including leave of absence from office. In which case, the LGC categorically provides that the Vice-Mayor shall exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive, except for the conditions clearly provided therefor. On the other hand, Section 46 (c) thereof, as above-cited, presupposes a situation where the local chief executive, like the Municipal Mayor, is traveling within the country but outside his territorial jurisdiction for a period not exceeding three (3) consecutive days, in which case, an OIC of the office of the local chief executive may be designated. A perusal of the subject Order shows that the reason for her [Mayor Layus] designation of SB Member Agpuldo as OIC is because of her leave. Accordingly, it is this Department's view that what is applicable in the herein case is Section 46 (a) of the Code. This Department opines that using Section 46 (c) of the Code to which such designation was anchored appears to be misplaced. Consequently, it can be opined that the ramifications of the transactions that may have transpired during such period are deemed to be void ab initio. As referenced in your letter, Mayor Layus has not been holding her office in the municipal hall for over a year now, ostensibly due to her health condition. Given her condition, Mayor Layus may avail of leave privileges pursuant to Section 81 of the Code, specifically last paragraph thereof, subject to pertinent rules of the Civil Service Commission. However, if Mayor Layus insists in continuing to hold office not in the municipal hall, as clearly provided in Section 444 (c) of the Code2, she may be held administratively liable. In such case, the appropriate remedy is to institute an administrative case with the Sangguniang Panlalawigan pursuant to Section 61 of the Code. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. 1 Section 81. Xxx. Elective local officials shall be entitled to the same leave privileges as those enjoyed by appointive local officials, including the cumulation and commutation thereof. 2 Section 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. (c) During his incumbency, the municipal mayor shall hold office in the municipal hall.

Very truly yours: BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: Underse GAN ry for Local Government DIRECTOR JONATHAN PAUL M. LEUSEN, JR., CESO Ill DILG-Region II Regional Government Center, Carig Sur, Tuguegarao City HON. CELIA T. LAYUS, MD. Municipal Mayor Claveria, Province of Cagayan LLLS/RPB,'LRALLD/27
